A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLE-Live and CoMind. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the methods, results and displays. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A-H. The substantial revision does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original experiments on 20 past competitions, a public-resource ablation, submissions to four ongoing competitions and human novelty assessments.

after.justification: Sections 5-7 report CoMind results on 75 past and eight ongoing competitions, alongside the retained 20-task evaluation. The appendices add original code analyses, resource measurements, validation trajectories and case studies.

M1.justification: v1 specifies a four-stage loop with idea/report pools and report-level collaboration. v2 expands the specified system to share kernels, datasets and checkpoints through a resource-dependency graph, and introduces dedicated evaluation and execution-monitoring components. These change shared state, coder inputs and execution control beyond merely assigning names to existing roles; the underlying ideation and ReAct loop remains.

E1.justification: The 20-task, seven-category evaluation expands to all 75 MLE-Bench competitions across low, medium and high difficulty, covering additional requirements such as segmentation, object detection and question answering. The original four live competitions are replaced by eight different competitions, including MABe Behavior, Impostor Hunt and RSNA Aneurysm. The original 20-task coverage remains as an ablation study.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds comparisons with Neo, R&D-Agent, ML-Master, OpenHands and MLAB, using attributed leaderboard results. AIDE and its Code/RAG variants remain in the 20-task comparison. The live evaluation replaces v1's AIDE comparison with comparisons against the strongest public kernels.

E3.justification: v1's principal setting uses 4 vCPUs, five hours per competition, one hour per execution and 20 implementation steps. v2's main setting specifies 32 vCPUs, 24 hours, five-hour executions, 30 steps per coder and four parallel agents. Its main leaderboard comparison includes heterogeneous backend models, whereas the retained 20-task study keeps a common o4-mini backend and the five-hour/4-vCPU budget. Appendix A also introduces additional code-quality metrics.

E4.justification: The public-resource ablation and retrospective time-course analyses are retained. v2 adds cyclomatic complexity, Pylint and Halstead analyses, live validation trajectories, a kernel-vote distribution analysis, an Impostor Hunt failure analysis and a detailed denoising workflow case study. Conversely, v1 Section 5.5's expert assessment of solution novelty is removed; automated code-complexity measurements assess a different question.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly reports means and standard deviations for token usage and cost across 75 competitions, including cost of $32.25 ± $19.43. Appendix H discloses seed 42 in example splitting and training code. These additions do not establish additional repeated runs; benchmark performance still lacks repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds a 36.00% medal rate on 75 tasks, compared with Neo's 34.22%, and new live standings averaging top 7.35%. These are expanded or replaced evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1. The retained category win rates are unchanged, including CoMind's 0.668 overall. Human novelty rankings and explicit valid-submission results disappear. Code-length assignments also change: image-classification AIDE changes from 5192.1 to 4624.3, with AIDE+Code receiving the former AIDE value; the PDFs do not explain this apparent label swap.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 newly defines the evolving community state (K_t, D_t, T_t) and a resource-dependency graph T_0 = (V, E), adding a formal representation of relationships absent from v1's idea/report-pool account. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees, and v2 adds no theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MLE-Live, CoMind and community-driven iterative exploration. v2 emphasizes specialized multi-agent collaboration and updates the headline performance claims to the full benchmark and new live competitions. It drops v1's explicit contribution claim about overcoming context-window limitations and its introductory human-evaluation endorsement. These refine the contribution framing while preserving the central research thesis.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about contamination from public datasets and failure caused by unreliable popularity signals, validation on only ten examples, saturated feedback and inadequate component assessment (Appendix F). It also attributes live progress to distinct exploration and refinement phases. v1's report-only interaction limitation and broader-impact discussion are removed, while the earlier explanation of Seq2Seq failures under runtime constraints remains.

D1.justification: Appendices G-H add role prompts, evaluator scripts' specifications, 90/10 splitting and stratification instructions, monitoring prompts, generated code and detailed example hyperparameters. Appendices B and E add token/cost measurements and per-competition resource inventories. These greatly expand documentation beyond v1's brief setup. However, v1's explicit CoMind code-release statement and repository link are omitted; this does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to ML-Master, R&D-Agent and Wuchty et al.'s study of teamwork, and positions CoMind against newer competing systems. The worked example also references CBAM. The main related-work discussion and its distinction between isolated agents and community-aware research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark description and method exposition are extensively rewritten, and the title gains the CoMind prefix. The former unified experimental section is reorganized into benchmark evaluation, ablation and analytical sections, with substantial supporting material organized into Appendices A-H. This changes the narrative structure beyond simply appending new results.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the workflow diagram and replaces the introductory radar chart with paired comparison plots. It adds difficulty-based benchmark tables, live leaderboard displays, validation trajectories and resource visualizations. The original ablation table is incorporated into a revised bar chart that omits the valid-submission panel, while the code-length table is expanded and moved into Appendix A.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evaluation coverage and sparse operational documentation through the full 75-task evaluation, detailed prompts and code, evaluation instructions, cost reporting and concrete failure analysis. These make generality, implementation and failure boundaries much more assessable. The gains outweigh the loss of the human novelty study and code-release link, although the apparent code-length label swap weakens reporting reliability. The heterogeneous-backend leaderboard comparison also leaves the architecture's independent contribution unresolved.
